question: What is the primary clinical objective when managing acute watery diarrhoea in children?

options.A: Preventing and treating dehydration until the illness resolves
options.B: Restricting oral fluid intake to allow the bowel to rest
options.C: Stopping stool output immediately with strong anti-motility drugs
options.D: Administering broad-spectrum antibiotics to clear all gut bacteria

explanation: Acute watery diarrhoea is typically self-limiting, so the main goal of treatment is maintaining fluid and electrolyte balance rather than stopping the diarrhoea. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h1)

question: A child with frequent watery stools rapidly develops hypovolemic shock primarily due to which factor?

options.A: Severe accumulation of toxins in the brain
options.B: Massive loss of water and essential electrolytes
options.C: Complete cessation of red blood cell production
options.D: Sudden failure of the heart muscle pump

explanation: Rapid fluid and electrolyte depletion reduces circulating blood volume, leading directly to hypovolaemia and potential shock. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h1)

question: Oral Rehydration Therapy primarily treats dehydration by utilizing the intestinal absorption of which two substances?
explanation: The active transport of glucose across the intestinal wall drags sodium and water along with it into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h2)

question: Why is Oral Rehydration Therapy considered superior to intravenous therapy for mild to moderate dehydration in community settings?

options.A: It works ten times faster than any intravenous fluid line
options.B: It requires sterile surgical theaters and specialized doctors
options.C: It is inexpensive, safe, and can be given by caregivers at home
options.D: It completely kills all viral pathogens living inside the gut

explanation: The accessibility and ease of administration make ORT ideal for early community-level intervention without needing venous access. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h2)

question: Which specific protein in the gut helps absorb glucose and sodium together?
explanation: SGLT-1 is the specific transport protein responsible for cotransporting sodium and glucose into the enterocyte. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h3)

question: Why does oral rehydration therapy remain effective even during severe secretory diarrhoea caused by toxins?

options.A: Oral salts directly neutralize all bacterial poisons in the colon
options.B: The SGLT-1 transport pathway remains functional despite toxin action
options.C: Secretory toxins completely destroy the lining of the stomach
options.D: Water absorption relies entirely on active gastric acid production

explanation: Even when secretory channels are overactive, the sodium-glucose cotransport mechanism in the small intestine operates independently. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h3)

question: What is the total osmolarity of the current WHO-recommended reduced-osmolarity ORS solution?
explanation: Reduced-osmolarity ORS lowers sodium and glucose levels to achieve a total osmolarity of 245 mmol/L. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h4)

question: What was the main clinical advantage of shifting from standard high-osmolarity ORS to reduced-osmolarity ORS?

options.A: It significantly decreases stool volume and intravenous infusion needs
options.B: It speeds up the destruction of parasites in the large intestine
options.C: It completely eliminates the taste of salt for young children
options.D: It allows the solution to be stored safely at room temperature for years

explanation: Lowering the osmolarity reduced the risk of osmotic diarrhoea and hypernatraemia, decreasing both stool output and IV fluid requirements. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h4)

question: A child who is lethargic, has very sunken eyes, and a skin pinch that goes back longer than two seconds is classified with which condition?
explanation: Lethargy, very sunken eyes, and a prolonged skin pinch are classic signs indicating severe dehydration requiring emergency intervention. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h5)

question: A mother brings her irritable toddler to the clinic with sunken eyes and a skin pinch that returns slowly. What level of dehydration does this indicate?
explanation: Irritability, sunken eyes, and slow skin recoil are diagnostic markers for 'some dehydration', managed under Plan B treatment guidelines. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h5)

question: What is the consequence of mixing an ORS packet in significantly less water than recommended?

options.A: It completely stops all vomiting episodes within five minutes
options.B: It turns the liquid into a fast-acting antibiotic medication
options.C: It creates a hypertonic solution that can worsen dehydration
options.D: It safely doubles the speed of cellular waste elimination

explanation: Too little water increases the solute concentration, drawing water out of the intestinal mucosa and aggravating fluid loss. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h6)

question: Why should nurses recommend feeding ORS using a clean cup and spoon instead of a feeding bottle?

options.A: Spoons allow the child to absorb the salt directly through the tongue
options.B: Spoons ensure the child drinks the entire liter of fluid in one gulp
options.C: Feeding bottles completely block the glucose transport mechanism in the gut
options.D: Feeding bottles are harder to keep clean and introduce bacteria

explanation: Feeding bottles easily harbor pathogens that worsen diarrhoeal illness, whereas cups are much easier to clean and keep hygienic. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h6)

question: What is the recommended daily dose of elemental zinc for a child who is two years old with acute diarrhoea?
explanation: Children aged six months to five years receive 20 mg of elemental zinc daily for 10 to 14 days. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h7)

question: Why is zinc supplementation continued for 10 to 14 days after the acute diarrhoeal symptoms have stopped?

options.A: To permanently numb the gut wall against all future viral infections
options.B: To restore intestinal mucosal integrity and prevent future episodes
options.C: To act as a strong sedative helping the child sleep through the night
options.D: To serve as a replacement for oral rehydration salt solutions

explanation: Continued zinc administration rebuilds damaged gut lining and strengthens immunity, reducing the recurrence of diarrhoea for months. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h7)

question: What is a suitable alternative fluid to give at home if commercial ORS packets are not immediately available?
explanation: Safe household fluids like rice water or clean water help maintain hydration while caregivers seek formal medical care. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h8)

question: What is the primary role of nurses in community education regarding diarrhoeal diseases?

options.A: Replacing all traditional healers with licensed medical doctors
options.B: Forcing every household in the village to build an indoor pharmacy
options.C: Distributing free intravenous infusion kits to every mother in town
options.D: Empowering caregivers to recognize early dehydration and prepare ORS correctly

explanation: Community education equips mothers and caregivers with practical skills to start rehydration safely at home before complications develop. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h8)
